newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia's key hydroelectric plant restarts.
newsitem.headline: Georgia's key hydroelectric plant restarts.

text.p: Georgia's Inguri hydroelectric power station, which generates almost half the country's needs, has resumed operations after a three month stoppage for repairs, a Fuel and Energy Ministry official said on Tuesday.
Georgi Makashvili, deputy director of state-owned Gruzenergo, said the station was now producing between eight and 10 million kilowatt hours of electricity per day.
Repairs had cost the state 4.5 million lari ($3.4 million) but had only patched over problems which will eventually require $60 million to eliminate.
Inguri is in the western part of the country near Georgia's breakaway region of Abkhazia.
